## Why this matters

Case fatality shows the proportion of patients admitted with a heart attack or stroke who die before leaving hospital. It is an important outcome indicator, influenced by how quickly patients reach care, their severity and comorbidity, and the care they receive. Falling rates may reflect improvements in detection, treatment, or recovery support, while rising rates may point to delayed presentation, older or more complex patients, or hospital strain. Tracking these trends helps reveal whether hospital outcomes are changing over time.
